extracted.intended_audience: high-net-worth philanthropists and potential Giving Pledge signatories; people interested in large-scale philanthropy
extracted.subtask_description: Making the Giving Pledge: a public promise by very wealthy individuals to give the majority of their wealth to charitable causes (during their lifetime or via wills), and participating in the Giving Pledge community and its learning/impact activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promise to give the majority of one’s wealth
rubrics_metrics.description: The Giving Pledge is a promise by the world’s wealthiest philanthropists to give the majority of their wealth to charitable causes in their lifetime or wills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core requirement/commitment of the initiative: wealthy individuals publicly commit to directing the majority of their wealth toward charitable causes either during life or through their estate. The page frames this as the defining promise of signatories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit a pledge letter explaining commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories provide a 'pledge letter'—a personal statement describing their reasons for pledging and their philanthropic intent (examples are shown: e.g., 'I cannot think of a more personally rewarding ... give while one is living').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pledge letters convey personal motivation and intent; the site presents short exemplar excerpts from pledge letters by signatories (Benoit Dageville and Marie-Florence Dageville, Nikhil Kamath, Charles F. Feeney). The letters function as a public articulation of the pledge and may demonstrate urgency, responsibility, or approach to giving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the Giving Pledge community (learning, connecting, action)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Giving Pledge is described as a global community that actively connects signatories to one another and to changemakers—'learning and engaging deeply to drive progress on the most urgent issues around the world.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signatories are expected (or encouraged) to participate in community learning sessions, share ideas, and collaborate. The site lists 'Learning sessions' and examples (e.g., 'Optimizing for the promise of AI in education'), signaling an orientation toward collective learning and exchange of practices among members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give at scale with an impact orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Giving Pledge signatories are described as 'giving at scale and with great impact—from shifting philanthropic norms to seeding innovations and helping people and communities thrive.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pledge emphasizes significant, impactful philanthropy rather than small-scale donations. Impact is framed broadly (norm change, innovation, community thriving). Prospective signatories should intend to make large-scale contributions and emphasize outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of causes and methods of giving is acceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatories 'span generations, support an array of issues, and give in a multitude of ways—what unites them is a shared promise and a commitment to creating an impact.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Giving Pledge does not prescribe a single cause area or mechanism for giving; rather it accepts varied issue focuses and giving strategies. The unifying criterion is the scale/majority-wealth commitment and an explicit commitment to impact, not a particular policy area or giving vehicle.
